paragraphs.en: My lady, my father was a king with a brother also ruling as a king. My cousin, his son, and I grew close in friendship and affection. One day, he treated me kindly, offering sheep and clear wine.
paragraphs.zh: 我的 Lady，我父亲曾是一位国王，他的兄弟也同为国王。而我的堂兄和他的儿子与我情谊深厚。有一天，他对我十分友善，送给我羊羔和清澈的美酒。

paragraphs.en: When we were drunk, he revealed a secret he had prepared for a year: to take a woman into a sepulcher in a graveyard. He swore me to secrecy before leading us there. Inside the sepulcher, my cousin brought water, mortar, and an adze.
paragraphs.zh: 当我们喝得酩酊大醉时，他透露了一个精心筹备了一年的秘密：要带一名女子到墓地里的一个石室中。在向我发誓保密之后，他带着我们前往那个地方。进入石室后，我的堂兄带来了水、灰浆和凿子。

paragraphs.en: He broke open a tomb, revealing a hidden staircase beneath an iron plate. The lady descended, and my cousin asked me to replace the plate and earth after he followed her down.
paragraphs.zh: 他撬开了一个墓穴，发现铁板下藏着一段暗梯。那位女士走了下去，我的堂兄让我在他之后下去后将铁板和泥土恢复原状。

paragraphs.en: The next evening, Dinarzad urged her sister Shahrazad, "Sister, please tell us one of your delightful stories!" King Shahrayar chimed in, asking for the continuation of the king's son's tale. Shahrazad replied with enthusiasm.
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，迪纳兹达催促她的姐姐沙赫拉扎德：“姐姐，请给我们讲一个你那些精彩的故事吧！”国王沙哈雷亚尔也附和着，希望继续听王子的故事。沙赫拉扎德热情地应允了。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad recounted: After following the dervish’s instructions, I returned home hungover and spent the night at my uncle’s house. In the morning, I couldn’t recall what happened the previous night, thinking it was just a dream. I inquired about my cousin but received no answers.
paragraphs.zh: 沙海拉扎德讲述道：按照那位苏菲圣士的吩咐回家后，我醉醺醺的，当晚便在叔叔家过夜。第二天早上，我对前一晚发生的事情毫无印象，以为只是个梦。询问起我的表弟，却未得到任何回应。

paragraphs.en: Wandering through graveyards, searching for his sepulcher, I found nothing. Nightfall brought increasing worry as I recalled our events bit by bit, like remembering a dream. I returned home, ate lightly, and had an uneasy night.
paragraphs.zh: 游荡在墓地之间，寻找我的安息之地，却一无所获。夜幕降临，思绪渐渐纷乱，仿佛在回味一场梦境。我返回家中，简单吃了些东西，整晚都感到不安。

paragraphs.en: The following morning, I revisited the graveyard, searching until nightfall without success. Over three more days, I searched from dawn till dusk but still found no clue. Frustration and worry nearly drove me mad.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天一早，我又回到了那个墓地，直到夜幕降临仍一无所获。接下来的三天里，我从黎明到黄昏不停地搜寻，但依然没有找到任何线索。沮丧和焦虑几乎让我疯狂。

paragraphs.en: Finally, realizing there was no other choice, I decided to return to my father’s city.
paragraphs.zh: 最终意识到别无选择，我决定返回父亲所在的城邦。

paragraphs.en: Upon entering the city, I was immediately attacked and bound. The vizier had plotted against my father, killing him and seizing power. He ordered his men to ambush me.
paragraphs.zh: 一进城，我就遭到突然袭击并被绑了起来。原来那位 vizier 早就对我父亲图谋不轨，暗中害死了他，并夺取了权力。他命令手下伏击我。

paragraphs.en: As it happened, our enmity dated back to when I shot an arrow that hit him instead of a bird he was watching from his palace roof.
paragraphs.zh: 恰巧的是，我和他的仇怨要追溯到他从宫殿屋顶上注视着的一只鸟被我射中的那一次。

paragraphs.en: When brought before the vizier, he gouged out one of my eyes with his finger and bound me in a chest. The vizier instructed my father’s swordsman to take me into the wilderness on horseback, kill me, and let beasts consume my flesh. The executioner followed these orders but was moved by my verses.
paragraphs.zh: 当他被带到 vizier 面前时，vizier 用手指挖出了我的一只眼睛，并将我关进了一个木箱里。vizier 命令我父亲的剑士骑马带我去荒野中，杀死我，然后让野兽吞噬我的肉身。刽子手遵照这些命令行事，但在看到我的诗篇后心生怜悯。

paragraphs.en: I recited:
paragraphs.zh: 我朗读道：

paragraphs.en: My shield I deemed you from the foeman's dart, But you did prove to be that very dart. I counted on your aid in all mishaps, Just as the left hand comes to aid the right. Stand then as one absolved, away from me, And let the foes at me their arrows aim, For if our friendship you cannot maintain, Between yourself and me there is no claim.
paragraphs.zh: 你曾是我的盾牌，抵御敌人的箭矢， 却没想到你竟是那支箭 itself。 我指望你在困境中相助， 犹如左手辅助右手一般。 如今，请你站远些，与我无关， 让敌人将箭射向我吧。 若我们的友谊无法维系， 我和你之间便再无瓜葛。

paragraphs.en: The executioner was moved by my verses and spared me. He advised me to flee and never return, warning that they would kill both of us. The poet adds:
paragraphs.zh: 刽子手被我的诗篇所感动，没有执行处决。他建议我逃走，永远不要回来，并警告说他们将会杀掉我们俩。诗人补充道：

paragraphs.en: If you suffer injustice, save yourself, And leave the house behind to mourn its builder. Your country you'll replace by another, But for yourself, you'll find no other self. Nor with a mission trust another man.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你遭遇不公，自救为上， 抛下这座宅第，莫为其建造者哀伤。 他乡即是故乡，但唯有自己才能救赎自我。 切勿将重任托付他人。

paragraphs.en: I barely trusted my own escape and kissed his hand. Losing an eye seemed preferable to death.
paragraphs.zh: 我几乎不敢相信自己逃过一劫，但仍吻了他一下手。失明似乎比死更可接受。

paragraphs.en: The lion, undaunted by his struggle, prowled with a mighty mane. His loyalty surpassed even mine.
paragraphs.zh: 这只狮子在搏斗中毫不气馁，鬃毛随风飘扬，显得威猛无比。他对忠诚的坚持甚至超过了我。

paragraphs.en: I traveled slowly until reaching my uncle's city. Upon meeting him and sharing the news of my father’s death and lost eye, he shared his own sorrow over a missing son. His words revived my grief, prompting me to recount what had happened to his son.
paragraphs.zh: 我慢慢行进了好一阵子，才抵达叔叔所在的那座城市。见到他后，我把父亲去世以及失明一事告诉他，他则流露出对失踪儿子的哀伤。他的话语勾起了我的悲痛，让我忍不住将发生在他儿子身上的事情一五一十地讲了出来。

paragraphs.en: He was elated and urged me to show him the sepulcher.
paragraphs.zh: 他欣喜若狂，催促我带他去看那座陵墓。

paragraphs.en: I confessed I had forgotten its location but agreed to accompany him. We secretly visited the graveyard, where I recognized the sepulcher. Descending fifty steps, we encountered thick smoke.
paragraphs.zh: 我承认已经忘记了那地方的位置，但还是同意陪他一起去。我们悄悄地来到了墓地，一眼认出了那个墓穴。下了五十级台阶后，我们遇到了浓浓的烟雾。

paragraphs.en: My uncle invoked God's name before we entered a hallway leading to a hall with high skylights and pillars. Inside, we found a cistern, large jars of flour, and a bed covered by a canopy.
paragraphs.zh: 我的叔叔在我们进入一条通向高窗和柱子的宽敞大厅的走廊前，念了上帝的名字。里面摆放着一个水池、装满面粉的大罐子以及一张铺着帐幔的床。

paragraphs.en: My uncle approached the bed, lifting the curtain to reveal his son and a woman lying together, now reduced to black charcoal. He expressed satisfaction, struck his son’s face, and declared their punishment in both worlds.
paragraphs.zh: 我的叔叔走近床边，掀起帷幔，露出他儿子和一个女子的尸体，此时已变成乌黑的炭块。他显得颇为满意，一巴掌拍在儿子脸上，并宣布了他们在人世与来世都将受到的惩罚。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad paused as morning came, but her sister Dinarzad praised her tale. Shahrazad responded that it was nothing compared to what she would tell the next night if she lived.
paragraphs.zh: 天边渐渐泛起了鱼肚白，沙赫拉兹德停下了讲述。然而她的妹妹迪纳兹德称赞起她刚才的故事来。沙赫拉兹德回应说，这故事比起她第二天晚上要讲的可就差远了。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad said to her sister Shahrazad, "Sister, if you are not sleepy, tell us one of your lovely tales." The king added, "It should be the completion of the first dervish's tale."
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳兹达对她的姐姐沙赫拉扎德说：“姐姐，如果你不困的话，给我们讲一个你那动人的故事吧。”国王补充道：“最好是完成那位第一位苦行僧的故事。”

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad replied, "With pleasure."
paragraphs.zh: 沙海拉扎德回答说：“遵命。”

paragraphs.en: She began: "I heard that when the uncle struck his son’s face after they lay in a charred heap, the dervish said, 'Uncle, for God’s sake, don’t make me feel worse. I am worried and sorry about your son’s fate, but you strike him again with your shoe as if he hasn’t suffered enough.' The uncle replied that his son was madly in love with his sister, despite his attempts to forbid it.
paragraphs.zh: 她开口说道：“我听说，当那位叔叔在一片焦黑中打完侄子的脸后，苦行僧说：‘叔叔，求求你了，别让我感到更糟。我很担心你儿子的遭遇，但你竟然还用鞋底抽他，仿佛他已经受够了痛苦似的。’那位叔叔则辩解说，尽管他曾极力阻止，他的儿子依然疯狂地爱上了自己的妹妹。”

paragraphs.en: When they grew up, they committed a terrible deed, which the uncle heard about and punished severely. He said, 'Beware of this deed; our story might spread far and wide, dishonoring you among kings.' The uncle secluded her but she remained in love with him, driven by the devil.
paragraphs.zh: 他们长大后犯下了一桩可怕的罪行，叔叔听说后严厉地惩罚了他们。叔叔警告说：“切记此事；我们的故事可能会传遍王宫，让你蒙羞。”尽管叔叔将她软禁起来，但她依然深爱着他，被恶魔所驱使。

paragraphs.en: The dervish continued: "When they were separated, he built a subterranean place, dug up a well, and brought provisions. He took his sister when I wasn’t around and did what you saw. He believed God would forgive them, thinking he could enjoy her for a long time."
paragraphs.zh: 德维什继续说道：“他们分开后，他在地下建了一个隐蔽的地方，挖了一口井，并备足了食物。他趁我不在的时候带走了妹妹，做了你们看到的事情。他认为上帝会宽恕他们，相信自己可以和她共度长久时光。”

paragraphs.en: They wept together, remembering the uncle’s loss of his son and brother, as well as the dervish’s own eye. They climbed out of the tomb, replaced the iron plate cover, and returned home undetected.
paragraphs.zh: 他们一同泪流满面，想起那位叔叔失去儿子和兄弟的悲痛，还有圣士自己失明的眼睛。随后他们从墓穴中爬出，重新盖上了铁板盖子，并悄悄返回了家中。

paragraphs.en: We barely sat down when we heard the sounds of kettledrums, little drums, trumpets, and the din of battle. The air was thick with dust from galloping horses and tramping men. My father's kingdom had been seized by a vizier who had gathered his armies, including bedouins, and launched an unexpected attack on our city.
paragraphs.zh: 我们刚一坐下，就听见铜鼓、小鼓、号角声和战阵的喧嚣。空气中弥漫着骏马飞驰和士兵踏步扬起的尘土。父亲的王国被一位 vizier 掌控了，他集结了包括贝都因人在内的大军，对我们城市发起了出其不意的攻击。

paragraphs.en: My uncle fell in battle, while I escaped to the outskirts, fearing for my life and that of Sayir, my father’s swordsman.
paragraphs.zh: 我的叔叔在战斗中阵亡，而我则逃到了城外，生怕自己和父亲的剑客赛伊尔也会遭遇不测。

paragraphs.en: My sorrows deepened as I thought about what had happened to my family and the loss of my eye. If I showed myself in public, people would recognize me and try to gain favor with the vizier by killing me. The only way out was to shave off my beard and eyebrows, change into a mendicant's clothes, and assume the life of a dervish.
paragraphs.zh: 想到家人遭遇的不幸以及自己失明一事，我的忧伤更甚了。如果我出现在众人面前，人们肯定会认出我来，并试图博得 vizier 的好感而暗害于我。唯一的出路就是剃掉胡须和眉毛，换上乞丐的衣服，过起苦行僧的生活。

paragraphs.en: I left the city undetected and journeyed to this country, hoping to reach Baghdad where I might find someone who could help me meet the Commander of the Faithful. This night, as I stood at the city gate in doubt, two other strangers approached—dervishes like myself—and greeted us. We walked together under the cover of darkness, three strangers without a clear direction.
paragraphs.zh: 我不声不响地离开了城市，踏上了前往这里的旅程，希望能抵达 Baghdad，在那里或许能找到一位能帮助我见见至高哈里发的人。就在这个夜晚，当我站在城门口犹豫时，有两位陌生人走了过来——像我们一样的苦行僧，并向我们打了招呼。我们在夜色的掩护下并肩同行，三个人都没有明确的目标和方向。

paragraphs.en: God led us to your house, and you were kind enough to let us in. As we sat by your hearth, you helped me forget my troubles, including the loss of my eye and the shaving off of my beard.
paragraphs.zh: 上帝引领我们来到了您的府上，您也够仗义，让我们进了门。在您温暖的炉火旁坐定后，您的话让我暂时忘却了烦恼，包括我失明的一只眼睛和剃光的胡须。

paragraphs.en: The girl told Dinarzad, "Stroke your head and go." But he replied, "I won't leave until I hear the tales from the other dervishes."
paragraphs.zh: 女孩对迪纳扎德说：“摸摸你的头，走吧。”但他回答道：“我不会离开，直到听完了其他苏菲圣士的故事。”

paragraphs.en: Morning arrived, and Shahrazad fell silent. Then Dinarzad said to her sister, "Sister, what an entertaining story!" Shahrazad responded, "Wait till tomorrow night; my tale will be even better if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹德默不作声。迪纳兹达对妹妹说：“姐姐，你的故事真精彩！”沙赫拉兹德回答道：“等明天晚上吧；如果国王饶恕我，我的故事会更好听。”

paragraphs.en: The king thought, "I'll delay her execution until I hear all the dervishes' tales."
paragraphs.zh: 国王心想：“我先暂缓她的执行死刑，等听完了所有圣士的故事再说。”

paragraphs.en: On the fortieth night, Dinarzad asked Shahrazad, "Sister, tell us one of your stories if you're not sleepy." Shahrazad agreed, saying, "With pleasure."
paragraphs.zh: 在第四个夜晚，迪纳兹达对莎赫拉兹德说：“姐姐，如果你不困的话，给我们讲一个你的故事吧。”莎赫拉兹德欣然应允，说道：“乐意之至。”

paragraphs.en: The caliph praised the first dervish's tale, declaring it stranger than any he had heard. Then the second dervish stepped forward to share his story.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发称赞第一位苦行僧的故事，宣称比他听过的任何故事都要离奇。随后，第二位苦行僧走上前来分享他的故事。
